answer: One registered treasure find backs one identity: a detectorist sweeps an island field for a landowner, files finds; inquest plus museum accession tie one hoard to one finder; the vault holds it, the registry re-checks yearly and refuses a second claim. Each fake costs $7,000 and 365 days: detector $3,000, land and inquest $4,000. One hundred fakes cost $700,000 and 36,500 days. Cheapest cheat: an unreported hoard for $4,000, but it has no inquest title, the seller surrenders their own record, and a nebula-bright fake fails the patina assay, so it buys a void hoard, not an identity.
